newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: French wounded in Ethiopia blast evacuated.
newsitem.headline: French wounded in Ethiopia blast evacuated.

text.p: A French couple wounded in one of two grenade blasts in Addis Ababa on Saturday were evacuated by plane to Paris on Monday for treatment, diplomats said.
Two Britons who were also injured in a grenade blast in a restaurant in the capital were still being treated in a hospital emergency ward, hospital sources said.
A doctor at the Russian-run Baltcha Hospital in Addis Ababa said on Monday the French woman was injured in one of her eyes and the French man had been wounded by shrapnel in his legs.
An Ethiopian waitress was killed and 42 people including four Britons and a French couple were wounded in Saturday night's attacks on the chic Italian restaurant and a hotel.

Two wounded British men said they were in Ethiopia to train the police and threw themselves at one of the grenades to protect their wives. They were in Blue Tops, an expensive Italian restaurant favoured by foreigners and rich Ethiopians.
Ethiopian police said a waitress died and 33 people were wounded when a grenade was lobbed into the Tigray Hotel near the busy Piazza area in the city centre, at about the same time.
The blasts appeared to be the latest in a series of politically motivated bombings in Addis Ababa and provincial cities.
President Meles Zenawi's government blamed Moslem fundamentalists for several bomb attacks last year. Ethiopian authorities remain secretive about their investigations.

British, French and German tourists were wounded last February in a grenade attack on a hotel in the ancient walled city of Harar in the east. Last November, hijackers believed to be Ethiopians seized an Ethiopian Airlines plane and forced it to ditch off the Comoro Islands, killing 125 people on board.
Last August Ethiopian troops backed by the air force raided alleged Moslem fundamentalist bases in western Somalia. The Horn of Africa country has both Christians and Moslems.

The government has bad relations with neighbouring Sudan and accused Khartoum of helping to plot the failed assassination attempt against Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak when he visited Addis Ababa in June 1995.
